title: What If Your AI Agent Never Had to Leave the Browser? (Demo 🚀)
why_read: An update on WebMCP, an experimental browser API letting websites expose tools directly to AI agents, relevant to those tracking agentic web standards.
analysis: WebMCP is described as an experimental browser API that lets a website explicitly declare tools an AI agent can call, essentially bringing the Model Context Protocol idea (used for LLM tool-calling) into the browser itself. The bulk of this piece is personal conference-recap fluff about the author's talk rather than substantive technical explanation, with a pointer to an earlier, now partly outdated article for details. For readers wanting to understand WebMCP itself, this post is mostly a teaser rather than a deep technical explainer.
